samples.question: The image shows one thick dark corridor on a plain background. The corridor is a single connected shape built from six long horizontal bays; each bay is a solid rectangle, the six bays sit at six different heights, no two bays overlap in height, and every bay has its own uniform thickness, measured as its height. No two bays are equally thick. Bays are stitched together by short vertical connectors that all share one common narrow width, much narrower than any bay is thick and much shorter than any bay is long; a connector may run past a bay it does not join, and where it does it stays clear of that bay. The bays and connectors form one single unbranched chain: exactly two bays are the ends of the chain and each of the other four bays is joined by connectors to exactly two bays. A hollow green frame stands in clear background just beyond one free end of one of the two end bays, and that bay is the start bay. Walk the chain from the start bay, stepping through connectors from bay to bay until the far end bay is reached, and read off the thickness of each bay in the order the walk meets it. This walking order is the only order that counts; it is not the top-to-bottom order of the bays. Light gray squares are decoration and mean nothing. Counting only bays after the start bay, how many bays on this walk are thicker than every bay met earlier on the same walk? Answer 1, 2 or 3.
